body:
## What this PR does
This PR is the release branch of CamCraft 0.28.0. It merges into `main` after the cut gate is green and after an independent review.

- `RECOMMENDED.md` gets the 155 decision files of the cut under one `v0.28.0` heading. The files are removed from `docs/decisions/`.
- `RELEASE_NOTES.md` has the 0.28.0 notes: breaking changes, upgrade notes, changes to posted G-code, highlights, known issues and process changes.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has one 0.28.0 row for each behaviour PR merged since v0.27.0.
- `cargo xtask release --version 0.28.0 --no-tag --skip-gate` set the version to 0.28.0 in `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`.

## Cut list
The cut line is 2026-11-27T20:59Z (the maintainer's answers in the question dialog).

In the cut:
- #4133 / PR #4440: the site tests in the gate. Merged as d5544b6f5.
- #4341: the Z retract before a tool change. PR #4509 supersedes PR #4371. Merged as 740b44133 on 2026-11-28.
- #4431 / PR #4405: the red `main` (the two `wire_post` tests write into a temp folder). Merged.
- Always in a cut: a fix for a red `main` or a red cut gate.

The maintainer added these PRs after the cut line ("Include them, then freeze"; "yeah include both"):
- #4410, #4449, #4423, #4424, #4368, #4441 and #4438.

These seven PRs merged into `main` after the freeze notice, between 00:01Z and 00:02Z on 2026-11-28. They stay in the release, and the release notes name them:
- #4467, #4298, #4442, #4425, #4458, #4459 and #4460.

Out by decision: #4312, and #4383 (kernel to `main`, merges after the tag).

No other PR merged into `main` after 2394b5ad1 except PR #4509.

## Known issues
Each open `P1` and `P2` issue that is not on the cut list is in the "Known issues" section of `RELEASE_NOTES.md`. A comment on this PR lists them.

## What did not run
- No Windows machine: the pixel-snapshot lanes and the Windows per-OS readings did not run.
- The cut gate has not run: no online cut runner has zola and node.
- The local package step of `cargo xtask release` stopped at phase 8 (`package-linux: missing rpmbuild`). The release build and the post version check (0.28.0) passed. `release.yml` builds the published packages from the tag.

Changelog: none (release mechanics)

title: feat(app): rename a tool with its operations in one undo step
body:
Stacked on #4482 - do not merge before #4482.

## What changed

- New command `RenameTool { from, to }` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_rename.rs`). It sets the new `Name` on the tool entity and the `tool` field of each operation that uses the tool. This is one undo step. The entity stays, so the tool keeps its definition, number, holder body, drawn cutter and component stack.
- A name is not an input of a toolpath. An operation that is Ok before the rename gets its stamp again, so it stays Ok. A Stale operation stays Stale.
- `RenameTool::new` refuses by name, before the history:
  - an empty name (after a trim) or a control character;
  - an unknown name, or an entity that is not a tool;
  - the same name;
  - a name that another entity has, or that a setup reserves;
  - a name that an operation still names (the operation of a deleted tool must not take this tool);
  - a name that the machine reserves (`tool_reservations::for_tool_as`).
- New MCP tool `rename_tool { name, new_name }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/tool_rename.rs`). It runs the same command. The rows in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and in the site guide are added.
- The Name row of the tool library editor is a text field (`tool_tab.rs`). The typed name is a draft of the window (`ToolLibraryView::rename`). Apply queues `RenameTool` after the other draft commands. A typed name makes the draft dirty, so Duplicate (#4482) waits for Apply. Cancel drops the typed name. A refused name keeps the typed text.
- The views follow a renamed tool (`crates/ui/src/state_tool_rename.rs`, called once in `drain_actions`): the library editor, the Properties target and draft, and the tool shape window. A view follows only when it still shows the old name that was recorded before the commands of the frame ran, and the same entity now has a new name. Thus a view that moved to another tool (Duplicate opens the copy) stays, and a rename of another tool does not move it. This covers Apply, undo, redo and an agent's `rename_tool` (the MCP host runs inside `drain_actions`).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/4370-rename-tool.md`.

## Tests

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/rename_tool.rs` (in the existing `tool_library_holders` suite, no new test binary):
  - `rename_moves_the_tool_and_its_operation_in_one_undo_step`
  - `a_stale_operation_stays_stale_through_a_rename`
  - `rename_refuses_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
  - `mcp_rename_tool_runs_the_command_and_undo_restores_it`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_rename.rs` (a module of the `camcraft-ui` lib tests):
  - `the_name_row_is_a_text_field_and_typing_is_a_draft`
  - `apply_renames_the_tool_and_its_operations_in_one_undo_step`
  - `a_rename_of_another_tool_leaves_the_open_editor_alone` (Duplicate, then a rename of the copy, its undo and its redo: the editor stays on its tool)
  - `an_empty_name_is_refused_and_cancel_drops_the_typed_name`
- `layout_window_tool_editor` asserts the Name text field.
- The existing `tool_library_frame::duplicate_opens_the_copy_and_is_one_undo_step` stays green: the follow law does not pull the editor back from the copy.

The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui`: 2021 on the parent head 6189d81, 2025 on this head.

Gate on the final head b7878b42547eeb9c37667fcca4e183229a922d78 (lanes, log `gate-4370-b7878b425.log`):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 394 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (43.0 min). One SKIP: `site tests` (the lane has no `zola`); this is not a pass for the site guide row
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (exit 0)

The base of the quick gate is `origin/main`, so the plan also covers the commits of #4482.

No post, toolpath or geometry changed, so no example catalog suite and no light lane step applies. This is a `P7` PR, so no heavy step.

## Not exercised

- A rename from a live MCP client against a running window. The ui test drives the same `CommandKind::RenameTool` path, and the MCP host runs inside `drain_actions`.
- The cut recipe library, machine reservation files and exported `.camtools` files keep the old name. They are outside the document. A recipe that names the old tool is refused by name when it is used (see the decision file).
- Unapplied field edits in the library editor are read again from the tool when an undo or an agent renames the open tool.

## Screenshots

The draw code of the editor did not change after these renders.

Before (the Name row is a label):

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4510/before.png)

After (the Name row is a text field with a typed new name):

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4510/after.png)

Changelog: Tool library: the tool editor can rename a tool. Each operation that uses the tool follows the new name in the same undo step. The MCP tool `rename_tool` does the same for agents.

Effort: max (escalated from high after two red quick gates; this head has the fixes and a new pin for the follow law)

Fixes #4370

title: fix(post): retract Z before a later tool change's G49 (mazak, fanuc, doosan)
body:
Supersedes #4371 (take-over, author mkinney; commits kept). This branch starts from the #4371 head `ce23fdaa8`. It then has one merge of `origin/main` and one fix commit. There is no rebase and no force-push.

## What changed

- The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts lift Z before the preamble of each section after the first (commit `ce23fdaa8`, mkinney).
- The lift uses the `safeRetract` method of the post: `G91 G28 Z0` (default) or `G53 G00 Z<safeRetractZ>`.
- The lift comes immediately before the `G90 ... G49 G80` block. The `G90` of that block ends the `G91` of the `G28` lift. `T M6` and `G43 H` follow as before.
- The first section gets no lift. Single-tool programs do not change.
- A Go home or a setup-change lift already raises Z. The post then writes no second lift (`zUp` flag).
- Fanuc and Doosan: a tilted section leaves `G43.4` armed until the next `G49`. The post then writes `G49` before the lift, in the same order as its Go home. The upright return after a tilt (#3466) does not write its own lift now.

## Take-over work (the findings of the review of `ce23fdaa8`)

1. **Stale recorded program, red suite.** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc` is regenerated (see "Recorded programs moved").
   - Class rule: I ran each `camcraft-app` suite with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, and `cargo xtask catalog --case` for each red catalog case and for the two heavy catalog cases.
   - Then a script read each tracked `.nc` file. It found no Fanuc, Mazak or Doosan program that has a later `G49 G80` block without a lift before it. The programs that it still finds are Tormach and Haas programs. Those posts are out of scope (follow-up #4372).
2. **Conflict with main.** I merged `origin/main` into the branch. Main changed the same preamble lines:
   - `fanuc.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`: main (#4346) added `G17 G94` to the preamble block. The merge keeps the #4341 lift before the block and the #4346 words in the block.
   - Main (#4348) added its own `tcpmLeft` flag for the program end. The two changes use the one flag: the section end sets it, and the next preamble or `onClose` reads it. The merge keeps the one declaration of main and removes the duplicate declaration of #4371.
   - Main moved the post test files into directory suites. The two new test files of #4371 moved with them: `crates/post/tests/script_wcs/setup_change/tool_change_retract.rs` and `crates/post/tests/script_rotary/upright_after_tilt/tool_change_retract.rs`.
   - Recorded programs: the merge takes the text of main, and the fix commit regenerates them.
3. **Notes (not blocking), also done.**
   - The decision record now has the setup-change stop case after a tilted section, and the shared `tcpmLeft` flag.
   - `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` ("The laws every post states") now states the lift.

## Recorded programs moved

All are Fanuc programs, because the default post is Fanuc. No Mazak or Doosan recorded program has a later section. Each `+n` is `n` new `G91 G28 Z0` lines. Each new line is between the `(OPERATION: ...)` note and the `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80` block of a later section. No other line changes.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc`:
  - section 2 (after an upright section): +1.
  - section 3 (after the tilted section): the order changes from `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80` / `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90` to `G49` / `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80`. `G00 A0. B0.` follows as before. TCPM is off before the `G28`, and Z is up before the preamble block.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_grid_by_part.nc` (+6). This file is new on main since #4371.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/fanuc_linear_by_tool.nc` (+2). This file is new on main since #4371.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/program_entry/fanuc_pause_home.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc` (+1)
- `examples/first-part.nc` (+2), regenerated with `camcraft-cli process`
- `examples/catalog/2d/adaptive-pocket/adaptive-pocket.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work/edge-work.nc` (+3)
- `examples/catalog/2d/first-part/first-part.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/2d/hole-work/hole-work.nc` (+4)
- `examples/catalog/2d/slots/slots.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/3d/rest/rest.nc` (+1). This case is new on main since #4371.
- `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish/rough-finish.nc` (+2)
- `examples/catalog/probing/probe-face/probe-face.nc` (+1)
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: two places change in the same way as section 3 of the deburr program. They change from `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80` / `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90` to `G49` / `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90 G17 G94 G54 G40 G49 G80`.

The regeneration also rewrote some files that this fix does not change. I reverted them, and they are not in this PR:
- `.camproj` files: the project `version` changed from 83 to 84.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`, `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc`, `docs/tester-kits/*.camproj`, `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, `examples/first-router-part.camproj`: the last digit of some A words and feeds changed (for example `A-39.432` to `A-39.431`). The Tormach post is not changed. The suites of these files pass on the committed text.

`crates/app/tests/program_entry.rs`: `z_homes` counts trip homes. It does not count the new lift immediately before a preamble `G49` line. The tests keep their intent (commit `ce23fdaa8`).

## Tests

Pinning tests:
- `script_wcs`: `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g28`
- `script_wcs`: `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g53`
- `script_wcs`: `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_the_same_tool_called_again`
- `script_wcs`: `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_trip_home_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `script_wcs`: `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_setup_change_stop_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `script_rotary`: `upright_after_tilt::tool_change_retract::fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract`
- `app`: `mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post` (`the_three_section_tilthead_program_matches_its_golden`), the suite that was red in the review.

The #4371 body records the red-before-fix check and the mutation results. The review of `ce23fdaa8` repeated the mutations.

Gates on the final head (`4f6526650`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 723 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The step `site tests (python unittest, zola, node)` is SKIP (zola and node are not installed on this host). This is not a pass. The post suites `script_wcs` and `script_rotary` and each `camcraft-app` suite are in the plan.
- Example catalog suites: `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `first_part_programs`: pass (in the quick plan).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 4 steps, 0 failed.
- Targeted heavy step (P1 under the safety floor): `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --only "app heavy: example_catalog"`: 1 step, 0 failed. It holds the heavy tests of the recorded programs that this fix moves: `catalog_2d_slots::{regenerates,rebuilds}` and `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::{regenerates,rebuilds}`, 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The first two quick runs stopped at `post build (--no-run)` with E0463 (stale build artifacts of `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-kernel`). I did not change code between the runs. I ran `cargo clean -p` on those crates and ran the gate again with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

## Not exercised

- No run on a Mazak, Fanuc or Doosan control.
- After a tilted section, the post writes `G49` before the lift, as its Go home did before. On a control where `G49` alone moves Z, that `G49` still runs before the lift. It is in the same place as before this PR. The post does not lift first, because a reference return under TCPM can alarm.
- No Mazak golden program with two tools. The word-level pins cover the order. The review of `ce23fdaa8` accepted this.
- Haas, Tormach and LinuxCNC also write `G49` in each section preamble. They are out of the scope of this issue (#4372).
- `crates/ui/tests/catalog_render.rs` and the site tests did not run.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4341-mazak-retract-before-toolchange.md`.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Changelog: The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts lift Z by the safe retract method before each later tool change, so the G49 of the next preamble never runs at the clearance height of the previous operation.

Fixes #4341

title: feat(ui): fold chips keep a glyph when short, count warnings, test Blocked and Not generated
body:
Stacked on #4492 - do not merge before #4492.

## What changed

Follow-up of the pre-review of #4492. Four points of #4503.

- `fold_chip` now paints the glyph alone when the state text does not fit. When not even the glyph fits and the state needs attention, it paints a warn bar at the chip's foot. Only a clean chip stays bare. A pane too short for the title still shows only the folded mark. The text stays in the tooltip.
- The Browser chip counts the warnings of the cached toolpaths ("4 warnings"). It reads them as the tree row reads them. An operation with warnings is therefore not "Up to date" on the chip.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/4483-pane-fold.md` says why a leaf with several tabs shows the state of its active tab only.
- Tests for the blocked and the never-generated state on both chips.

No change to toolpaths, posts or the project file. No command, so no MCP tool.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft_ui_kit::fold::tests::a_short_pane_paints_the_glyph_alone_not_nothing` (full text, glyph only, warn bar, bare clean chip).
- `camcraft_ui_kit::fold::tests::an_attention_chip_paints_a_state_below_its_title_at_every_height` (drives `fold_chip`, reads the painted shapes: a state text or the warn bar under the title) and `a_clean_chip_paints_no_warn_bar_and_no_warn_ink`
- `egui_app::tests::pane_fold::a_never_generated_operation_shows_on_both_folded_chips`
- `egui_app::tests::pane_fold::a_blocked_operation_shows_on_both_folded_chips`
- `a_stale_operation_shows_on_the_folded_browser_chip` is changed: the seed has warnings, so the chip shows the exact count (a literal 89 pins the counter), not "Up to date". The blocked test now pins the exact text "1 blocked · N warnings", so the order is pinned.

## Gate

Base for the gate: `refs/remotes/qsmits/issue/4483-side-pane-fold` (head `1bca29cc9`), so that only the commits of this PR count.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base <that ref>` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui-kit -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: both green on head `137fbb13e` (review fix: warn bar, exact-text tests).
The `#[test]` count of `crates/ui` goes from 2032 to 2034. `camcraft-ui-kit` has one test more.
No snapshot PNG changed.

## Screenshots

In the light theme `warn_ink` is 1.92:1 on the chip ground (below 3:1). UI plan A (#4485) adds the `status_warn` token. The bar and glyph switch to it there. See the decision file.

title: fix(contour): accept natural endpoint picks on open centerlines
body:
## Change and scope

An open 2D Contour now accepts a start pick that exactly equals its natural centerline endpoint.
Climb uses the first stored point; conventional travel uses the last.
The pick does not shift, trim or reverse the run. Every automatic move stays the same.

The app path supports one selected open DXF sketch chain with Side Auto and no side override.
Its source is the cutter centerline, which proves the endpoint identity.
The existing climb XOR per-chain reverse setting determines the start.
The existing WCS mapping rotates the pick with its geometry.

Named refusals remain for interior, opposite-end and nearby picks; unproved part and stock source mapping;
offset or extended open boundaries; multiple selected sketch chains when an open chain is present;
open-chain exit picks; and the existing tilted-contour cases.
The part source refusal also covers its no-material fallback.
This is the natural-centerline part of item 5. The remaining source and tilted mapping work stays open under #1473.

Decision: [1473-open-chain-end-picks.md](https://github.com/seelesturm/Camcraft-NeoTech/blob/26872c796815c2babd330a01ff19a82a494cf04b/docs/decisions/1473-open-chain-end-picks.md).
The issue adds nine tests and extends the existing short-terminal-leg test without weakening its geometry assertions.
The app tests join existing binaries through child modules. No new test binary is added.

## Reproduction before the fix

Canonical baseline: `6898b02ea3195e9124e6113afd6ab3cee38d0c50`.
Input: centerline `[(0, 0), (20, 0)]`, Lead None, climb enabled, start pick `(0, 0)`;
top 10, bottom 0 and stepdown 5.
Expected: accept that natural endpoint and preserve every automatic move.

```text
cargo test -j 2 -p camcraft-motion --lib machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_open_chain_accepts_a_start_pick_at_its_natural_end -- --exact
```

The independent baseline build succeeded. The test exited 101: zero passed, one failed, 790 filtered out.
It failed at `contour_run_side_tests.rs:67:52` with:

```text
natural end is a valid start: Invalid("start point (0.000, 0.000): an open chain starts at its end - a picked start is taken only on closed contours yet; clear the start point")
```

The loop stopped before its conventional case. The fixed pin retains that assertion and exercises both directions.
The exact 14-line test-only baseline patch is archived with the phase 6 evidence.

`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=2`, worktree-local target and no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.

- `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_offset_part_run_refuses_unproved_source_start_picks`
- `machining2d::contour_run_side::tests::an_open_run_with_a_short_leg_at_an_inside_corner_stops_clear`
- `machining2d::contour_run_stock::tests::an_offset_stock_run_refuses_unproved_source_start_picks`

body:
## What changed

- A new undoable command, `FaceToSize` (`crates/app/src/commands/face_to_size.rs`), faces a block to height from numbers.
- The command holds two steps in one `BatchCommand`:
  - an optional `SetStock`: a box of the stated size, with its top at the top Z;
  - a normal `CreateOperation`: a Face on `SrcRef::Stock`, from the top Z down to the final Z.
- The Face uses `top_z` (first stage), `cut_z` (final Z) and `stepdown` (depth per pass). It also uses the stated stepover, cut direction, feed and plunge feed.
- One undo removes the Face and the stock that the step set. A step that keeps the existing stock does not remove it.
- The Z values are program Z. The command adds the world Z of the active setup's placed WCS (0 when no WCS is placed). It stores the heights as `Fixed` world Z.
- The command refuses these inputs by name, at construction. A refusal changes nothing.
  - a final Z at or above the top Z;
  - a depth per pass, stepover, feed or plunge feed that is not more than 0;
  - a stock size that is not three numbers more than 0;
  - an empty or unknown tool;
  - a stepover wider than the tool (ribs stay between the rows);
  - no stock and no stock size;
  - a top Z below the stock top (the first pass would cut deeper than the depth per pass);
  - a final Z at or below the stock bottom (the face would cut through the block).
- A new MCP tool, `face_to_size` (`crates/app/src/mcp/face_to_size_tools.rs`), runs the same command through the session history.

title: fix(ui): a gauge length edit never draws the library body over wider steel
body:
Stacked on #4469 - do not merge before #4469.

## What changed

The generic component editor redraws a holder after a gauge length edit. It found the built-in holder by `library_ref`, id or name (`holder_entry`), and drew that holder's outline at the new length. A user holder with a library name and a wider body under the flange envelope then got the library body. That body is thinner than the real steel, and the outline goes into the collision checks.

- New `ComponentGeometry::regauged_holder` (`crates/tools/src/component_geometry_regauge.rs`). It gives the built-in outline at the new gauge length only when both conditions are true:
  - The holder's outline is the built-in holder's outline at the holder's own gauge length.
  - The new outline is the old outline with one straight cylindrical section made longer or shorter. The nose keeps its shape from the nose face, the flange keeps its shape from the gauge line, and the section keeps its old radius.
- Each other case is refused by name, and nothing changes:
  - `NotLibrary`: a library name on another outline.
  - `NoSection`: the outline shows no body section. This is a shrink chuck whose body the flange envelope covers, and also its look-alike with a wider hidden body. The two outlines are the same, so both are refused.
- `component_edit::build` uses the new function. The edit stays one undoable `EditDocumentComponent`.

title: fix(post): G43.4 posts write the joint angles of the A/B tilt chain
body:
## What changed

The Fanuc post and the Doosan DNM post wrote the stream's pose letters as the `A` and `B` words under `G43.4`.
The pose law is `axis = Ry(B)·Rx(A)·Z` (`crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`).
On the tilt head (`assets/machines/tilthead.mch`), the A rotary carries the B rotary, so the machine reads the words as `Rx(A)·Ry(B)·Z`.
When A and B both turn, that is a different tool axis. The check did not see it.

This PR makes the posted words the joint angles of the machine's own chain:

- `crates/post/src/post/tilt_chain.rs` (new): a prelude function `chainAngles(p)` that every post script sees. It reads the nest of the A rotary (about X) and the B rotary (about Y) from `machine.rotaries` (`parent`, `turnsPart`) and solves the joint angles when A is the outer factor.
- `crates/post/src/machine/tilt_chain.rs` (new): the same rule in Rust, `joint_angles(machine, letters)`.
- `crates/post/src/machine/judge.rs`: `pose_problems` judges the joint angles against the travel, not the letters. The check and the post read the same angles.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: `tilt()` calls `chainAngles` and writes its angles back on the record, so the feed cap and the held angles use them too.

The rule:

- A pose that turns at most one of A and B keeps its letters exactly (the two products are then the same rotation).
- The outer factor is the parent rotary in a head chain, the rotary nearest the work in a table chain, and the table in a table-and-head machine. B outer: the letters. A outer: solved again.
- Away from B = 90 deg there are two solutions. The first one that both travels hold is used, else the principal one (B in -90..90). The travel check then refuses it by name.

Refused by name, in the post and in the check, with the same text:

- A and B both turn and the machine does not state which rotary carries the other.
- A rotary of the A-and-B pair is stated along -X or -Y and turns.
- C turns as well on a chain where A is the outer rotary.

Other posts: I searched every post in `assets/posts/` for the same pass-through. Only `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` write stream A and B words under RTCP. `mach4.cps` solves its own AC trunnion. `tormach.cps` has a lone A. `linuxcnc`, `richauto`, `sinumerik-810m` and `heidenhain-klartext` refuse tilted moves. Only `tilthead.mch` has two tilting rotaries in `assets/machines/`.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/4417-tilt-chain-joint-angles.md`.

## Changed recorded programs (one by one)

Each change is the old wrong axis replaced by the joint angles. I checked each by hand with `Rx(A)·Ry(B)·Z`.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc`: `A16.78 B-47.983` -> `A24.251 B-45.342`, `A16.78 B47.983` -> `A24.251 B45.342`. The lone `A-16.78` of the two other corners becomes `A-24.251` (B stays modal, the same value).
- `examples/catalog/multiaxis/indexed/indexed.nc`: the Tilted pocket `A30. B30.` -> `A33.69 B25.659`. The `.camproj` did not change (the rebuild bumped only its version field, from main's format; I did not commit that).
- Test expectations: `post_engine::vendor_mch_cli` (`A30 B15` -> `A30.867 B12.953`), `program_units` (`A-45 B12.25` -> `A-45.66 B8.629`), `example_catalog` (`catalog_multiaxis_indexed::posts_two_single_axis_indexes_and_one_tilted_pocket` reads the posted joint angles).
- `setup_align_multiaxis`: its hand-built bench machine stated no nest, so the check now refuses its poses. The bench now states "B carries A" (the pose law's own nest). Its programs do not change.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/script_rotary/tilt_chain_joints.rs` (new module of the `script_rotary` suite; test names `script_rotary::tilt_chain_joints::…`):

- `fanuc_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b` and `doosan_dnm_posts_the_joint_angles_of_a_chain_where_a_carries_b`: post poses with A and B not zero on `tilthead.mch`. The forward kinematics of the posted words equals the stream axis within 1e-4. The check's `joint_angles` equals the posted words.
- `a_chain_where_b_carries_a_posts_the_pose_letters`: the same poses on the swapped nest post the letters, and the axes agree.
- `a_chain_with_no_stated_nest_is_refused_by_name`
- `the_machine_check_judges_the_joint_angles_not_the_letters`
- `a_pose_past_ninety_takes_the_second_solution_inside_the_travel`

Red first: with the posts of main (`git checkout 392980120 -- assets/posts/fanuc.cps assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`), the three post tests fail (log `gate-4417-eae2d557a-red.log`).

## Gate (final head 87ed4620f, Mac lane, `--pool`)

body:
## What changed

Step 1, PR P of the UI plan #4245. A docked pane folds to its title, so that the viewport gets the space.

- The fold flag is the `LeafNode::collapsed` flag of egui_dock. The fold arrow of the dock, the saved panel setups and the new fold law read this one flag.
- A pane in a top-over-bottom stack folds natively to its tab bar.
- A side pane (Browser at the left, Properties at the right) folds to a title chip, 28 points wide. The fold law keeps the open split fraction, holds the split at chip width on each frame, and puts the open fraction back on unfold. A window resize or a drag on the separator does not unfold or widen a folded pane.
- The shell draws the chip in the folded leaf, under its tab bar. The chip shows the pane title, turned to read from top to bottom. One click on the chip unfolds the pane. The fold arrow of the dock also unfolds it.
- Each chip keeps the safety state as text with a glyph (the #4245 E2 rule). The Browser chip shows the counts of blocked, stale and not generated operations, or "Up to date". The Properties chip shows the state of the open operation: "Up to date", "Needs regenerate", "Not generated" or "Blocked" (the reason is in the tooltip). The glyph is a check mark or a warning sign, so the state does not depend on colour. The sources are `status_of`, `stale_reason` and `tool_problem_of`, as in the tree and the operation page. Only a folded pane reads them.
- The chip hover is a 2 px accent frame and a full-ink title. The tooltip follows the pointer.

title: feat(tools): convert standalone tools to component stacks in one step, with a preview
body:
## What changed

A new command converts standalone document tools to component stacks in one undo step. The tool library window shows a preview first. An MCP tool has a dry run that returns the same preview.

- `crates/app/src/tool_convert.rs` (new): the plan. For each standalone tool it proposes a stack and gives a verdict:
  - the stack is: the tool's library holder as the built-in holder component, then a built-in collet that fits the holder and the shank (never a user adapter; none for a Weldon or shrink-fit holder), then the tool itself as a solid cutting item `user:tool:<name>`;
  - `same`: the stack derives the same tool record and gauge length, and the stack's holder body is the library holder body of the tool, bit for bit (the drawn profile and the bands);
  - `different`: the stack derives other values, and the row lists each difference;
  - `no match`: the row names the reason (no holder, no collet for this shank, a lathe tool, a stack that a `ChangeTool` law refuses, a stack holder outline that is narrower than the library holder anywhere).
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_convert.rs` (new): `ConvertToComponents`. It lands the selected rows in one undo step: the new table rows (built-in copies keep their library link), each stack, and each derived record and body. A `no match` row refuses the whole command by the tool name and the reason. Nothing changes then. `same_rows` selects every `same` row.
- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_assembly.rs`: `ToolUpdate` is `pub(crate)`, so the new command uses the same per-tool update as `SetToolAssembly`.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/convert_tools.rs` (new): `convert_tools_to_components { tools?, dry_run? }`. `dry_run: true` returns the preview rows and changes nothing. Without `tools`, only the `same` rows convert.
- UI: "Convert to components…" in the tool list header opens the preview in place of the list (`tool_library_dialog/convert.rs`, `state_tool_convert.rs`). Each row has a tick, the tool, the proposed stack and the result. Only the `same` rows start ticked. A `no match` row cannot be ticked. "Convert selected" queues one `ConvertToComponents`. "Select every row that converts" also ticks the `different` rows. The preview is computed on open, on Refresh and after a convert, never on a still frame. If the history moves after the preview, "Convert selected" is disabled until Refresh.
- An old library holder has the default stick-out: flute length plus shank length. Then no shank sits in the holder, and the stack resolver refuses it. For such a tool, the cutting item gets one shank diameter more of shank, and the gauge length stays the same. If the stick-out is longer than the whole tool, the longer shank also fills the gap to the holder nose. The new shank length is `projection - flute length + shank diameter`. The row is `different` and names the shank length change. The decision file gives the reasons.
- `tool_convert::outline_difference` compares the stack's holder body with the library holder body that the tool has now. It reads the bands as the collision laws read them (`tool_body::checked_profile`). A wider outline is a listed difference. A narrower outline is `no match`. Example: a tool whose holder reference has a longer gauge length than the library entry. The built-in holder component has the entry's own gauge length, so the stack's flange sits lower. Before this fix that row was `different` (gauge length). Now it is `no match`.
- A converted tool no longer counts as a user of its library holder (`library: None`). The holder view's "used by" count goes down. A later change of a built-in holder reaches the converted tool only by a sync of the holder component. The preview says this (`convert::LINK_NOTE`), and the decision file records it.

## Safety floor

This PR can change the holder body and the shank length that the collision checks read, and the tool lengths that the post reads. The rules that keep this safe:
- A row is `same` only when the tool record, the gauge length and the holder outline are all the same, bit for bit.
- A `different` row converts only when the user ticks it or names it. Its differences are listed (for example the longer shank, or a wider holder outline).
- A stack whose holder outline is narrower than the library holder anywhere never converts (`no match`). The collision checks never get a smaller holder.
- The longer shank of a shank-added row only adds steel. The gauge length stays, so the posted tool lengths stay.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and the site MCP guide name the new tool.
- `docs/decisions/4339-convert-to-components.md` records the decisions.

## Pinning tests

App, `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/convert.rs` (binary `tool_library_holders`):
- `convert::the_preview_names_each_verdict`
- `convert::the_same_rows_convert_in_one_undo_step_and_undo_restores_every_tool`
- `convert::a_different_row_converts_only_when_it_is_named`
- `convert::a_no_match_row_refuses_the_whole_command_by_name`
- `convert::mcp_dry_run_returns_the_preview_and_apply_converts_the_named_rows`

App, `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/convert_outline.rs` (same binary):
- `convert_outline::the_posted_program_of_each_converted_row_kind_does_not_change`: each tool has a generated Face operation. title: fix(post): honor rotary sign conventions in G43.4 output
body:
## Problem and change

Fix #4436 (P1, effort:high). A `table_rh` rotary needs the opposite sign from the tool-relative pose. Fanuc and Doosan DNM wrote `A30.` where the machine needed `A-30.`. The travel check also used the wrong sign on an asymmetric range.

Both G43.4 posts now apply the resolved convention when they write rotary words. The existing resolver uses the axis setting, then the machine setting, then `tool_rh`. The machine pose check uses the same signed angle. Its lone-X path applies the axis direction before the convention.

The default `tool_rh` program stays byte-identical. Modal angle memory, feed calculations, Mach4 and the chain solver do not change. No dependency, file format or process file changes.

Validated head: `3c0dc8eb7406aaaea4ccb752c8989c3e7c94284d`.

title: fix(post): retract Z before a later tool change's G49 (mazak, fanuc, doosan)
body:
## What changed

- The Mazak, Fanuc and Doosan DNM posts now lift Z before the preamble of each section after the first.
- The lift uses the `safeRetract` method of the post: `G91 G28 Z0` (default) or `G53 G00 Z<safeRetractZ>`.
- The lift comes immediately before the `G90 ... G49 G80` block. The `G90` of that block ends the `G91` of the `G28` lift. `T M6` and `G43 H` follow as before.
- The first section gets no lift. Single-tool programs do not change.
- A Go home or a setup-change lift already raises Z. The post then writes no second lift (`zUp` flag).
- Fanuc and Doosan: a tilted section leaves `G43.4` armed until the next `G49`. The post then writes `G49` before the lift, in the same order as its Go home. The upright return after a tilt (#3466) no longer writes its own lift.

## Cause

Each later preamble wrote `G49` and `T M6` at the clearance height of the previous operation. The Mazak EIA/ISO manual says that `G49` moves the axis to remove the length offset. Z could move down by the tool length, near the part. The `safeRetract` option text says "Z retract command before tool changes and at program end", but the post wrote it only at program end and on Go home.

Fanuc and Doosan had the same order. A FANUC-family control can move Z on a `G49` block with no axis word. The issue asks to fix the two posts or to record them as not affected. This PR fixes them.

## Tests

Pinning tests (new):
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g28`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_a_second_tool_g53`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::mazak_fanuc_doosan_retract_z_before_the_same_tool_called_again`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_trip_home_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `setup_change::tool_change_retract::a_setup_change_stop_is_not_followed_by_a_second_retract`
- `upright_after_tilt::tool_change_retract::fanuc_and_doosan_cancel_tcpm_before_the_tool_change_retract`

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code, the three `retract_z_before` pins fail with `left: 0, right: 1` (no Z retract before the second G49).

title: feat(mcp): list_posts, select_post, preview_post and save_post_script
body:
## What changed

This PR adds four MCP post tools (`crates/app/src/mcp/post_tools.rs`):

- `list_posts` lists each built-in post and each `.cps` file in the user posts folder. Each row gives the machine kinds that the post serves, `description`, `program_units`, `extension` and the declared options. A file that does not load gives its `problem`. `selected` is the document's post.
- `select_post` runs `SelectPost` through the session History. It is one undo step. `null` selects the default built-in post.
- `preview_post` runs a script (`source` or `path`) on a built-in sample (Facing, Contour, Pocket, Drilling) or on the document stream. It writes no file. It returns `ok`, `program`, `lines`, `warnings` and `swallowed`. A failed script returns `ok: false` and `errors` with the 1-based `line` in the script. The Boa runtime limits stop a script that loops.
- `save_post_script` saves a plain file name in the user posts folder. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`, else `<data dir>/camcraft/posts` (the same order as the user machines folder). The script must load and run before the save. An existing file is replaced only with `overwrite: true`. The write is atomic.

Other changes:

- In a live app session, `save_post_script` needs approval as a `FileWrite`, and `select_post` as a `LimitEdit` (`mcp::live::requires_approval`).
- A hidden test hook `Server::set_user_posts_dir` (an `Env` field) points the folder at a temp folder.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` is generated again (128 tools). `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` has the four rows. `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` has a "Post scripts" section.
- The decision file is `docs/decisions/2074-mcp-post-tools.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `mcp` suite, `post_tools::*` (6 tests):
  - `list_posts_lists_every_builtin_post_with_what_it_declares`
  - `select_post_is_one_undo_step_and_refuses_a_stranger` (undo and redo)
  - `preview_post_runs_a_script_on_a_sample_and_writes_no_file` (output, warnings, no file)
  - `preview_post_returns_the_1_based_line_of_a_syntax_error_and_stops_a_loop`
  - `save_post_script_writes_a_plain_name_into_the_user_posts_folder_only`
  - `a_live_session_asks_before_a_post_file_write_or_a_post_choice`
- `camcraft-app` lib: `mcp::post_files::tests::*` (folder order, plain names) and `mcp::post_tools::tests::the_error_line_reads_the_script_position`.

## Readings

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, head 362ab7198): 176 steps, 1 failed: `mcp_doc_drift` (`every_live_tool_is_in_the_guide_and_the_local_prompt`). The site MCP guide did not name the new tools. a8890b3a1 adds them; `mcp_doc_drift` (9 tests) and the `mcp` suite (62 tests) pass on the final head.
- Site tests (`python3 -m unittest discover -s site/tests`): no failure that main does not have.
- `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -p camcraft-app -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes: this diff changes no generator or post output.
- A real per-user data folder: the tests use a temp folder through the hook. The folder order is a unit test.

Process change: yes (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` gets the four tool rows, as the issue asks).

Changelog: MCP: `list_posts`, `select_post` (undoable), `preview_post` (read-only, no file written) and `save_post_script` (a plain file name in the user posts folder, `CAMCRAFT_POSTS`) tools for post authoring and selection.

Fixes #2074

title: feat(ui): add shared Help tips and read-only MCP discovery
body:
## What and why

Add Help > Tips and an optional tip on the start page for #3030.

- Keep four tips in `assets/tips/tips.json`. UI and MCP read that file.
- Add `list_tips` as a read-only tool. It does not change the document or undo history.
- Resolve the undo shortcut for the screen's OS. The MCP server uses its own OS.
- Keep the start tip below the normal actions. Hide it during generation, import, AI work and stock precalculation.
- Persist Don't show again in the existing per-user preferences. Help > Tips remains available and can restore the start tip.
- Open existing guide pages from Show me. Do not add new CAM actions or change output checks.

The undo tip distinguishes an attached agent from a headless document. The example tip does not promise a project for every operation.

## Tests and readings

Base: `1c0152c9106514622a641c17adc7520af45ebc6a`.

- Base RED: `list_tips_is_listed_and_read_only` failed because the tool was absent. The Help structural test failed because Help was absent.
- Sabotage RED: removing the new registry entry made the MCP pin fail again. Restoring it passed.
- GREEN: shared ids, four tip contents, source/response equality, repository link targets and Windows/Linux/macOS shortcuts.
- GREEN: Help window, shared text, guide action, named launcher refusal/recovery, screen OS shortcuts, nonblocking start tip, running generation suppression and persistent opt-out with synthetic preferences.
- GREEN: existing Home layout and the new Tips window layout.
- GREEN: selected quick gate, six steps: app lib, mcp, mcp_doc_drift, mcp_provider, view_prefs and ui lib.
- GREEN: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test mcp --test mcp_provider --test mcp_doc_drift --test view_prefs -- -D warnings`.
- GREEN: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- GREEN: focused site tests `test_release_027_batch3.py` and `test_ai_guide.py`.
- All four tip URLs returned HTTP 200. Tests also check their repository targets.

The selected gate command was:

```sh
CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3 CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main \
  --only 'app suites: lib' --only 'ui suites: lib' \
  --only 'app suites: mcp' --only 'app suites: mcp_provider' \
  --only 'app suites: mcp_doc_drift' --only 'app suites: view_prefs'
```

## Limits

The full quick plan selects 188 steps after MCP registration. The six directly affected steps above ran and passed. No post or toolpath changed.

The light dry-run selects 11 geometry twins and a full motion/app release build with `--no-run`. The assigned scope excludes that release rebuild for this UI-only change. The light lane was NOT RUN; it is not a reported pass. No full heavy, catalog or release gate ran.

Native tips rotate by UTC day. Browser builds use the first start tip without a native clock call. The Help window lists all tips. No browser build or physical machine was tested. The optional site Tips page is not added; no second text store exists.

Effort: medium
Changelog: Add Help tips, a persistent start-page tip preference and the read-only list_tips MCP tool.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3030#issuecomment-7203144792

## Before and after UI evidence

These native Linux captures compare the original base `1c0152c9106514622a641c17adc7520af45ebc6a` with the unchanged PR head `7f830a9fce69141dad90752ea4977fa5ef380d32`.

The four PNG files are on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `e6f6a3078e7bc3990a1d626bb6083f8c388958d5`. No image or source change was added to this PR branch.

### Help > Tips

No source, executable or image content was edited. This verifies its rendered appearance, **not successful automated Help-menu interaction**.

This update adds visual evidence only. The existing test results and their limits above remain unchanged; no broad suite was rerun.
